title: Flutter Linux host name parsing crashes on an empty PRETTY_NAME
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Verified against flutter/flutter master `53d381d9067f16b1d4132f5b8f059a9cc5ddb9ec`.

1. In an isolated Linux environment, set `/etc/os-release` to contain `PRETTY_NAME=`.
2. Run `flutter doctor -v`, which reads the operating-system name.
3. Also try `PRETTY_NAME="Linux=Example"`.

### Expected results

An empty name uses the existing Linux fallback; a name containing `=` is preserved.

### Actual results

Empty values cause a `RangeError` when the parser reads `value[0]`. Splitting at all equals signs also truncates nonempty names.

### Code sample

```text
PRETTY_NAME=
```

### Screenshots or Video

Not applicable to this tool parsing defect.

### Logs

The focused regression on unmodified production code reports 3 passed, 8 failed. The failure was reproduced using the repository's existing unit-test entry with fake processes or a memory filesystem. Unit tests use a memory filesystem and a fake Linux platform; they do not modify the host's system files.

A minimal fix with regression coverage is prepared. A draft PR will follow.
